newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand coalition talks stay in balance.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand coalition talks stay in balance.

text.p: Talks to form a New Zealand government hung in the balance on Wednesday, with Labour leader Helen Clark warning that political stalemate could drag on until February unless agreement was reached by next week.

Caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger told reporters after a meeting of his conservative National Party MPs it was still "50-50" whether nationalist New Zealand First would choose National or Labour as its coalition partner.
New Zealand First, led by charismatic Maori Winston Peters, was left holding the balance of power after an inconclusive general election on October 12.
A Labour spokesman said Labour and New Zealand First exchanged documents covering policies and the shareout of cabinet posts, and Clark and Peters later met for two and a half hours.
Asked how close the talks were to a resolution, Clark told reporters: "Either next week or February" -- a reference to the long summer break over Christmas and January.

She said Labour MPs were ready to meet at any time to decide on a coalition proposal. "We will let them know when we have something to discuss. They could be called at any time. They are on standby," she said.
Peters told reporters there would be more meetings with both National and Labour. "We're further down the track than we were last week...We are down to the outstanding issues."

New Zealand First was initially seen as closer to Labour on social policy and Maori issues, but views Labour's planned spending as excessive. Both agree the New Zealand dollar is overvalued and want to see it lower.

Media reports on Wednesday said Bolger's National Party, in power since 1990, was prepared to make sweeping concessions including scrapping a second round of planned tax cuts planned for July 1, 1997. Officials declined to comment.
Party leaders said it was still unclear when parliament would meet for the first time since the election, but it must do so by December 13.
